Dishes send $(l)FE through the air$(), where a conduit can't go. There is no beam: you can tell a $(l)Transmitter Dish$() is working because it turns to a receiver and $(l)holds still$() while it sends, and a $(l)Receiver Dish$() is getting power because the rings of its dish $(l)light up$() from the rim to the centre.

$(li)It is a small multiblock: place it with $(l)three Cyber Frames$(), on its right as you face it, behind it and in the corner between, and the dish unfolds on its turret over a 2x2 base. Alone, a right click sends out drones that show where they go.
pages.title: Transmitter Dish

pages.text: $(li)Feed it FE with $(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy Conduits$(/l) on the dish block. It takes in as much FE per tick as its module lets it send, and stores ten times that.$(br)$(li)Each Transmitter Dish has $(l)one network$(). In its GUI you give it a $(l)name$() and a $(l)colour$(), which lights the indicator on both dishes.
$(li)A new network is $(l)Private$(): only you and the players on your team can see it. Switch it to $(l)Public$() and anyone can link a receiver.

$(li)It serves up to $(l)4 receivers in turn$(): it turns to one (1 second), sends for 4 seconds, then moves to the next. The signal passes through blocks, but the chunks of both dishes must be loaded.$(br)$(li)A tenth of the FE is $(l)lost on the way$().
$(li)A small multiblock two blocks tall: put $(l)a Cyber Frame on top$() of it and its dish unfolds.
pages.title: Receiver Dish

pages.text: $(li)Its GUI lists the networks it can reach, with their colour, distance (or dimension) and seats taken, for example "2/4". Click one to link; a full network is greyed out. $(l)Disconnect$() leaves it. The GUI also shows the FE/t arriving.
$(li)It stores up to 2,000,000 FE and gives what it receives to the blocks and conduits around it.

The Transmitter Dish has one module slot. The module sets how far it reaches and how much FE per tick it sends in all, shared among its receivers.$(br)$(li)$(l)None$(): 32 blocks, 2,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module I$(): 128 blocks, 8,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module II$(): 512 blocks, 32,000
pages.title: Range Modules

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Range Module III$(): 2,048 blocks, 128,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Infinity Range Module$(): Unlimited, into other dimensions, Unlimited$(br)With a receiver in another dimension, both dishes point $(l)straight up at the sky$().
